course: Course 4: Operating Systems and Embedded Linux

chapters.title: How This Course Works, and Setting Up a Linux Lab
chapters.objective: Get a Linux system on any laptop, install gcc, QEMU and an ARM cross-compiler, and run one C program on two different processors.
chapters.lab: Cross-compile for ARM64 and run the result on an x86 laptop with qemu-aarch64.
chapters.board: Run the same binary on a Raspberry Pi over SSH.
chapters.toughest: Diagnose a broken toolchain from its error messages.

chapters.title: What an Operating System Does
chapters.objective: Explain the three jobs of an operating system (abstraction, isolation and sharing) by watching the Linux kernel do each one.
chapters.lab: strace a program, fork two processes with one address, crash safely, and share one CPU between two programs.
chapters.toughest: Explain, step by step, what happens when a program calls write().

chapters.title: Kernel Mode, User Mode and System Calls
chapters.objective: Understand privilege levels on x86 and ARM, and make system calls directly, without the C library.
chapters.lab: Write a program with no C library for x86-64 and for ARM64, and run both.
chapters.toughest: Write a static ARM64 program that prints and exits using only svc instructions.

chapters.title: Firmware, RTOS or Linux?
chapters.objective: Compare a superloop, a real-time operating system and Linux by memory protection, scheduling, footprint and boot time, and choose correctly.
chapters.lab: Build a tiny cooperative scheduler in C and measure its timing on the laptop.
chapters.toughest: Choose the operating system for a smart meter, a drone and a camera, and defend each choice with numbers.

chapters.title: The Shell and the Filesystem Tree
chapters.objective: Move around a Linux system confidently and know what lives where, including /proc, /sys and /dev.
chapters.lab: Explore /proc and /sys on the laptop and inside a QEMU guest.
chapters.board: Explore the Pi's /sys/class/gpio and /proc/device-tree.
chapters.toughest: Find any running process's open files and memory map from /proc alone.

chapters.title: Users, Permissions and Capabilities
chapters.objective: Control who may read, write and run every file, and give programs only the privileges they need.
chapters.lab: Create users and groups, set modes and capabilities, and write a udev-style rule.
chapters.board: Give a normal user access to the Pi's I2C bus.
chapters.toughest: Explain why a setuid program is dangerous and replace it with a capability.

chapters.title: Pipes, Redirection and Text Tools
chapters.objective: Combine small programs into pipelines that search, filter and summarise logs and data.
chapters.lab: Analyse a large device log with grep, sed, awk, sort and uniq.
chapters.toughest: Write a one-line pipeline that finds the five most frequent error codes per hour.

chapters.title: Shell Scripting for Engineers
chapters.objective: Write robust shell scripts that automate builds, tests and device setup.
chapters.lab: Write a script that builds, tests and packages a C project, and fails loudly.
chapters.toughest: Make a script safe against spaces, missing files and partial failures.

chapters.title: Building Software: Compilers, Make and Cross-Compilation
chapters.objective: Build C programs for the laptop and for ARM with gcc, Make and a sysroot, and inspect the results.
chapters.lab: Write a Makefile that builds for x86 and ARM64 from the same sources.
chapters.board: Deploy the ARM build to a Pi.
chapters.toughest: Explain every stage of a cross build and fix a wrong-architecture link error.

chapters.title: Libraries and the Dynamic Linker
chapters.objective: Create static and shared libraries and understand how the dynamic linker finds and loads them.
chapters.lab: Build a shared library, then trace the dynamic linker with LD_DEBUG.
chapters.toughest: Resolve a symbol-version conflict and explain lazy binding through the PLT.

chapters.title: Processes: fork, exec and wait
chapters.objective: Create, replace and reap processes, and understand the process life cycle.
chapters.lab: Write a tiny shell that runs commands and reports their exit status.
chapters.toughest: Explain zombie and orphan processes and prevent both.

chapters.title: Signals
chapters.objective: Send, catch and handle signals safely.
chapters.lab: Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM correctly in a long-running daemon.
chapters.toughest: Write an async-signal-safe handler and explain why printf is not allowed in one.

chapters.title: Threads
chapters.objective: Create and join POSIX threads and know what threads share and what they do not.
chapters.lab: Speed up a computation with threads and measure the gain.
chapters.board: Measure the same program on the Pi's four cores.
chapters.toughest: Explain exactly what a thread shares with its process and what it owns.

chapters.title: Scheduling
chapters.objective: Understand how Linux decides who runs next: time slices, priorities, nice values and CPU affinity.
chapters.lab: Measure how nice values and CPU pinning change running times.
chapters.toughest: Predict CPU shares under the Completely Fair Scheduler and the newer EEVDF scheduler for a given set of nice values.

chapters.title: Real-Time Scheduling
chapters.objective: Use SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR and SCHED_DEADLINE, and measure scheduling latency.
chapters.lab: Measure wake-up latency with and without a real-time priority.
chapters.board: Measure it on the Pi under load.
chapters.toughest: Explain priority inversion and how priority inheritance fixes it.

chapters.title: Virtual Memory and the MMU
chapters.objective: Explain pages, page tables, the TLB and address translation, on x86-64 and ARM64.
chapters.lab: Translate addresses by hand and check them against /proc/self/pagemap.
chapters.toughest: Walk a four-level ARM64 page table for a given virtual address.

chapters.title: A Process's Address Space
chapters.objective: Read a process's memory map and know where the code, data, heap, stack and libraries live.
chapters.lab: Watch a program's map change as it allocates and maps memory.
chapters.toughest: Explain copy-on-write after fork, with measurements.

chapters.title: Dynamic Memory in Embedded Systems
chapters.objective: Understand malloc, fragmentation and memory limits, and when embedded code should avoid the heap.
chapters.lab: Fragment a heap on purpose and measure the damage.
chapters.toughest: Design a fixed-block allocator with constant-time allocation.

chapters.title: Caches, DMA and Memory-Mapped I/O
chapters.objective: Access device registers from Linux, and use volatile, barriers and cache control correctly.
chapters.lab: Map a QEMU device's registers and drive it from user space.
chapters.board: Blink an LED by writing GPIO registers directly on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Explain why a DMA buffer needs cache maintenance and what goes wrong without it.

chapters.title: Files and the Virtual File System
chapters.objective: Use open, read, write and close well, and understand inodes, file descriptors and buffering.
chapters.lab: Measure the cost of unbuffered and buffered I/O.
chapters.toughest: Explain what happens to data between write() and the flash chip, and how to make it durable.

chapters.title: Filesystems for Flash
chapters.objective: Choose and configure filesystems for eMMC, SD cards and raw NAND, including read-only roots.
chapters.lab: Build and mount ext4, SquashFS and an overlay in QEMU.
chapters.board: Make the Pi's root filesystem read-only.
chapters.toughest: Design a root filesystem that survives sudden power loss.

chapters.title: Device Files, /sys and udev
chapters.objective: Understand character and block devices, major and minor numbers, sysfs and udev.
chapters.lab: Follow a device from /dev to its driver through /sys.
chapters.board: Follow the Pi's I2C controller the same way.
chapters.toughest: Write a udev rule that gives a USB serial adapter a stable name.

chapters.title: Talking to Hardware from User Space
chapters.objective: Drive GPIO, I2C, SPI and serial ports from Linux programs.
chapters.lab: Use QEMU's emulated serial ports and a simulated I2C sensor.
chapters.board: Read a real I2C temperature sensor and toggle GPIO with libgpiod.
chapters.toughest: Write a robust serial-port protocol handler with timeouts.

chapters.title: ioctl, poll and epoll
chapters.objective: Handle many devices and sockets in one program with event-driven I/O.
chapters.lab: Build an event loop that serves a serial port, a timer and a socket.
chapters.toughest: Compare select, poll and epoll for 10,000 connections and explain the difference.

chapters.title: Race Conditions and Mutexes
chapters.objective: Recognise data races and protect shared data with mutexes.
chapters.lab: Make a race visible, then fix it, with ThreadSanitizer.
chapters.toughest: Prove that a given locking scheme is free of races.

chapters.title: Semaphores, Condition Variables and Deadlock
chapters.objective: Coordinate threads with semaphores and condition variables, and avoid deadlock.
chapters.lab: Build a bounded producer-consumer queue.
chapters.toughest: Find and break a deadlock using lock ordering.

chapters.title: Atomics and Memory Ordering
chapters.objective: Use C11 atomics and understand acquire, release and the ARM memory model.
chapters.lab: Build a lock-free single-producer single-consumer ring buffer and test it on ARM in QEMU.
chapters.board: Test it on the Pi's real ARM cores.
chapters.toughest: Show an ordering bug that appears on ARM but not on x86, and fix it.

chapters.title: Inter-Process Communication
chapters.objective: Pass data between processes with pipes, FIFOs, message queues and shared memory.
chapters.lab: Compare the speed of four IPC methods.
chapters.toughest: Design a crash-safe shared-memory channel between two processes.

chapters.title: Sockets and Networking for Devices
chapters.objective: Write TCP and UDP clients and servers, and connect devices with MQTT.
chapters.lab: Build a sensor server and client and capture the traffic.
chapters.board: Publish the Pi's sensor readings over MQTT.
chapters.toughest: Handle partial reads, reconnects and back-pressure correctly.

chapters.title: From Power-On to Shell Prompt
chapters.objective: Follow the boot sequence: boot ROM, bootloader, kernel, init and the first program.
chapters.lab: Boot an ARM64 Linux kernel in QEMU and read every line of its boot log.
chapters.board: Read the Pi's boot log.
chapters.toughest: Explain what the kernel needs before it can run init, and what happens if it is missing.

chapters.title: Booting ARM Linux in QEMU
chapters.objective: Boot a kernel with an initramfs on QEMU's virt machine, and share files and networking with it.
chapters.lab: Build an initramfs by hand and boot it.
chapters.toughest: Boot a kernel with only one statically linked program and make it do useful work.

chapters.title: U-Boot
chapters.objective: Build and use U-Boot: environment, boot scripts, and loading a kernel over the network.
chapters.lab: Boot QEMU through U-Boot and load the kernel with TFTP.
chapters.board: Boot the Pi through U-Boot.
chapters.toughest: Design a boot script that falls back to a known-good kernel.

chapters.title: The Device Tree
chapters.objective: Read and write device tree source, and understand how the kernel matches drivers to hardware.
chapters.lab: Decompile QEMU's device tree and add a node.
chapters.board: Write an overlay for a sensor on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Describe a new board's peripherals completely in device tree source.

chapters.title: The Root Filesystem: BusyBox and init
chapters.objective: Build a minimal root filesystem with BusyBox and write the init process.
chapters.lab: Build a 2 MB root filesystem that boots in QEMU.
chapters.toughest: Write an init that mounts filesystems, starts services and reaps orphans.

chapters.title: Buildroot
chapters.objective: Build a complete embedded Linux system from source with Buildroot.
chapters.lab: Build and boot a Buildroot image for QEMU.
chapters.board: Build a Buildroot image for the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Add your own package and a custom kernel configuration.

chapters.title: The Yocto Project
chapters.objective: Understand Yocto layers, recipes and images, and when to choose Yocto over Buildroot.
chapters.lab: Build a minimal Yocto image for QEMU.
chapters.toughest: Write a recipe and a layer for your own application.

chapters.title: Your First Kernel Module
chapters.objective: Build, load and unload a kernel module, and read its messages.
chapters.lab: Build a module for the laptop and one for the QEMU ARM kernel.
chapters.board: Load it on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Explain what can and cannot be done in kernel context.

chapters.title: Character Device Drivers
chapters.objective: Write a character driver with open, read, write and ioctl.
chapters.lab: Write a driver for a virtual device and test it from user space.
chapters.toughest: Make the driver safe against concurrent readers and writers.

chapters.title: Platform Drivers and the Device Model
chapters.objective: Bind a driver to a device described in the device tree.
chapters.lab: Write a platform driver for a QEMU device.
chapters.board: Write one for a device on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Trace the probe path from device tree node to driver probe().

chapters.title: Interrupts, Bottom Halves and Workqueues
chapters.objective: Handle interrupts in a driver and defer work correctly.
chapters.lab: Write a driver that handles an interrupt from a QEMU device.
chapters.board: Handle a GPIO interrupt on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Choose between threaded IRQs, tasklets and workqueues for a given device, and justify it.

chapters.title: GPIO, I2C and SPI Drivers
chapters.objective: Write drivers on top of the kernel's GPIO, I2C and SPI subsystems.
chapters.lab: Write an I2C client driver for an emulated sensor.
chapters.board: Write it for a real sensor on the Pi.
chapters.toughest: Expose the sensor through the IIO subsystem.

chapters.title: Kernel Debugging
chapters.objective: Debug the kernel with printk, dynamic debug, ftrace and gdb through QEMU.
chapters.lab: Single-step the kernel in QEMU with gdb.
chapters.toughest: Find the cause of a kernel oops from its log alone.

chapters.title: PREEMPT_RT and Latency
chapters.objective: Build a real-time kernel and measure worst-case latency.
chapters.lab: Run cyclictest on a normal and a PREEMPT_RT kernel in QEMU.
chapters.board: Measure on the Pi under heavy load.
chapters.toughest: Find and remove a latency source with ftrace.

chapters.title: Profiling and Tracing
chapters.objective: Find where time goes with perf, ftrace and eBPF.
chapters.lab: Profile a slow program with perf and fix it.
chapters.toughest: Write an eBPF tool that measures a kernel function's latency.

chapters.title: Reliable Updates
chapters.objective: Update devices in the field safely with A/B partitions and rollback.
chapters.lab: Implement A/B updates with U-Boot and a QEMU disk image.
chapters.toughest: Design an update that survives power loss at any instant.

chapters.title: Secure Boot and the Chain of Trust
chapters.objective: Verify every stage from boot ROM to application, and know what TrustZone adds.
chapters.lab: Sign a FIT image and boot it with U-Boot verified boot in QEMU.
chapters.toughest: Find the weak link in a given chain of trust.

chapters.title: Power Management
chapters.objective: Use CPU frequency scaling, idle states and suspend, and measure their effect.
chapters.lab: Observe cpufreq and cpuidle behaviour on the laptop.
chapters.board: Measure the Pi's power draw in each state.
chapters.toughest: Design the power policy for a battery-powered device.

chapters.title: Capstone: An Embedded Linux Sensor Gateway
chapters.objective: Build a complete device: custom image, driver, service, network protocol and safe updates.
chapters.lab: Build and run the whole gateway in QEMU.
chapters.board: Build it on a Raspberry Pi with a real sensor.
chapters.toughest: Ship it: a reproducible image, a test suite and an update you can roll back.

chapters.title: Where Quantum Meets Embedded Linux
chapters.objective: See how quantum computers are controlled by FPGA boards running embedded Linux, and what an engineer does there.
chapters.lab: Run a pulse-sequencer simulation and talk to it the way control software talks to real hardware.
chapters.toughest: Explain the full path from a Qiskit circuit to microwave pulses on a qubit.
